description: far_skip_decode single-layer synthetic benchmark (pc40 GPU1 H20-3e, BF16, Qwen3 head_dim=128). Source: codex branch bench. This isolates the far-skip module, NOT model throughput or quality.

config.ring_capacity: sink(4) + near_len(4096) + window(128) + block_size(64) - 1 = 4551 theoretical; observed physical_tokens = 4415 (config/BF16 detail)
config.geometric_constant: evict physical_tokens (~4415) and kv_storage_bytes (~8.62 MB) are CONSEQUENCES of near_len/pages/budget/sink/window, INDEPENDENT of sequence length

key_observations.kv_independence_from_length: evict ring capacity (~8.62 MB/layer) is geometrically CONSTANT across 8K→128K — ring size depends only on sink+near_len+window+block-1, never on sequence length.

8K.note: ~2x faster than legacy path page-stat first-decode cost

128K.note: constant — compact selector scans bounded near pages, not full history

key_observations.evict_vs_retain_decode_ms: evict adds only ~0.12 ms/step vs retain (ring slot mapping overhead), negligible relative to KV savings.

comparative_context.E170c_theoretical: E170c prev analysis projected ~96% far KV elimination for budget K2 at long ctx (flow-based upper bound). This bench physically achieves 93-97% via finite ring.
comparative_context.capacity_overhead_ring_vs_dynamic: Ring reserves ~4551 positions = sink(4) + near_len(4096) + window(128) + block_size(64) - 1 = 4551, slightly EVCEEDING dynamic far_evict cap (1536 + 128 + 64 = 1728). This is a latency-for-simplicity trade-off.

caveats: Single-layer synthetic decode; not full-model throughput or quality.
NOT bitwise-equivalent to 4bit production TLI (different selector, different boundaries).
First-decode ms differs dramatically between runs due to cold page-summary build (retain=270ms @8K).
legacy arm was disabled in 128K run by bench config; 8K/32K/64K legacy data was obtained from separate earlier run.
eager-only; CUDA Graph capture is explicitly rejected by far_skip_runtime.
Batch size must be 1; beam/batching/offload unsupported.
